solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Board is liable to be damaged when picked up (8)

indicatorNotes.when picked up: to pick something up is to hear it, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: something liable to be damaged would chip

annotation.surface: A warning about a fragile panel that might get knocked when it is lifted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as lifting the board by hand; here it means caught by ear. Woodchip is board made from compressed chips of wood.
annotation.definitionFit: Woodchip is a kind of board made of bonded wood chips.

entries.clue: Extremely old ferries are fitted with propellers (5)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: only the extremes, the two end letters, of 'old' are used
indicatorNotes.ferries: to ferry is to carry, so OD carries ARE inside it

blocks.note: used as printed, carried inside O…D

annotation.surface: A remark about ancient passenger boats being refitted with engines and screws.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ferries' looks like the boats themselves but works as a verb: OD carries ARE. The propellers are oars, not ship's screws.
annotation.definitionFit: A boat that is oared has oars, the simplest propellers of all.

entries.clue: Really con agent with Dadaist fake (just one time) (4,7)

indicatorNotes.fake: a fake is a false version, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.just one time: of the two Ts (time = T) only one is allowed, so one T is dropped

blocks.note: AGENT with one of the two Ts dropped

annotation.surface: A swindle in which an agent passes off a forged piece of Dada art.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Con' is the opposite of pro here, not a swindle, and 'Really' intensifies it. AGENT and DADAIST share two Ts between them; the bracket keeps only one.
annotation.definitionFit: To be really con something is to be firmly opposed to it: dead against it.

entries.clue: Coastal town contains smart parts (8)

indicatorNotes.parts: STING parts HAS, splitting it in two by sitting in its middle

annotation.surface: A seaside town that holds some fashionable districts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contains' looks like the container instruction but only supplies HAS; 'parts' does the containing. Hastings is a town on the south coast of England.
annotation.definitionFit: Hastings is a seaside town in East Sussex.

entries.clue: Accomplices run to catch up as crossing border (8,2,5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry 'up' sends the letters upward, so they read backwards
indicatorNotes.crossing: RIM crosses SINCE, lying across it

blocks.note: as = since, as in 'as it's late'

annotation.surface: A fugitive hurrying to catch up with others as they cross a frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'up' belongs to R + ENTRAP and turns it into PARTNER.
annotation.definitionFit: Partners in crime are accomplices who act together.

entries.clue: Malcontent gambler cleared out with pained expression (6)

indicatorNotes.cleared out: the inside of 'gambler' is cleared, leaving its outer letters

annotation.surface: A bitter gambler, bankrupted, wincing at his losses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cleared out' fits a gambler who has lost everything; here it empties the word. A pained expression is something said, not a face.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name someone chronically dissatisfied and complaining.

entries.clue: Fabulous being in possession of European person’s make-up (6)

indicatorNotes.in possession of: to be in possession of something is to hold it, so GNOME holds E within its letters

blocks.note: a gnome is a creature of fable

annotation.surface: A fairy-tale creature holding a European's cosmetics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics; it means constitution, and a genome is the genetic kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A genome is the full genetic make-up of a person or organism.

entries.clue: Raising two daughters nothing unusual (3)

indicatorNotes.Raising: in a down entry, raising the letters makes them read from the bottom up

annotation.surface: A remark that bringing up two girls is quite ordinary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raising' reads as bringing up children, which the daughters encourage; it is the upward reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an odd event is out of the ordinary, as in 'that's odd'.

entries.clue: Attractive man on board (9)

blocks.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a chap
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

annotation.surface: A handsome crewman aboard a ship, or a good-looking director on the company board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as one idiom, aboard ship; split, 'on' just means placed above in a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Something covetable is attractive enough to be wanted.

entries.clue: Teetotal workmates eschewing opening spirits (6)

indicatorNotes.eschewing opening: the word avoids its opening letter, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a dry person drinks no alcohol
LADS, one's mates at work, without the L

annotation.surface: Colleagues on the wagon turning down the first round of hard liquor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' sits beside 'teetotal' as drink; it means supernatural beings. Dryads are tree nymphs of Greek myth.
annotation.definitionFit: Dryads are wood nymphs, nature spirits of Greek myth.

entries.clue: Pigeon very casually ignored swallows (8)

indicatorNotes.casually: done carelessly, so the letters of 'ignored' fall out of order
indicatorNotes.swallows: the rearranged word takes V inside it

annotation.surface: A pigeon casually ignoring the swallows sharing its sky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swallows' next to 'pigeon' looks like more birds; it is the verb that takes V in.
annotation.definitionFit: The ring dove, or wood pigeon, is a pigeon with a pale neck ring.

entries.clue: Girl rejected Spandex trousers (4)

indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the letters read in reverse
indicatorNotes.trousers: to trouser is to pocket, so 'Spandex' holds the answer inside it

annotation.surface: A girl turning down a pair of stretchy Lycra trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb here, pocketing the answer, not the garment the surface puts on the girl.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'girl' in crosswords stands for any female first name, and Edna is one.

entries.clue: Nameless boozer masters flayed (10)

indicatorNotes.flayed: a flayed thing has its skin stripped off, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub
DOMINATES with its first and last letters stripped

annotation.surface: An anonymous drunk who has thrashed his employers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like a drinker but is the pub, a common British sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal Latinate synonym, from in- (not) and nomen (name), used of things like the innominate bone.

entries.clue: Badly misrepresented yourself in penning article (11)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: shown falsely, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.penning: the rearranged letters pen, or enclose, A

annotation.surface: A writer who has misrepresented himself while penning a piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penning article' reads as writing a piece; it is a container around the grammatical article A.
annotation.definitionFit: To act nefariously is to act wickedly, badly.

entries.clue: Settler’s arrival met with displeasure (8)

blocks.note: arr. = arrival, as on a timetable

annotation.surface: A colonist's landing greeted with hostility by the locals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist; it is one who settles matters, an arranger.
annotation.definitionFit: One who settles or arranges things is an arranger.

entries.clue: Vulgar tackling church over singer’s morality (9)

indicatorNotes.tackling: RUDE takes on, or grips, the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.over: turned over, so CE reads EC

blocks.note: a tit is a songbird; the 's is ''s' = is, merely linking

annotation.surface: A crude critic taking on the church about a singer's moral standards.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer is a bird, not a vocalist.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rectitude, from Latin rectus (straight), is upright moral conduct.

entries.clue: They’re found with keys from bus regularly (4)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals: every other letter

annotation.surface: Lost property: things that turn up with keys left on the bus.
annotation.walkthrough: A fob is the fob on a key ring, often an electronic tag.
annotation.definitionFit: Key fobs are attached to key rings, so fobs are found with keys.

entries.clue: Player seems tall on Everton’s flanks (8)

indicatorNotes.flanks: the answer runs across the words and ends on Everton's flank, its first letter

annotation.surface: A report that a footballer looks tall playing out wide for Everton.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Player' sits among football words as a footballer; it is an actor, Sylvester Stallone. Everton is a Liverpool football club.
annotation.definitionFit: Sylvester Stallone is a film actor, a player.

entries.clue: Exploratory procedure cut short (4)

indicatorNotes.cut: cut off the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: SCANT = short, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A medical investigation abandoned before it was finished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' is one phrase in the surface; split, 'short' is SCANT and 'cut' docks it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an MRI or ultrasound scan is done to look inside the body and find out what is wrong.

entries.clue: Shut away at home, became vocal (8)

indicatorNotes.vocal: spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

annotation.surface: A recluse who stayed indoors and then found a voice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Became vocal' reads as speaking up; 'became' is TURNED and 'vocal' says to hear it.
annotation.definitionFit: The interned are confined, shut away, especially in wartime.

entries.clue: Establish new radio is faulty (6)

indicatorNotes.faulty: a faulty thing is broken, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A complaint that a brand-new radio doesn't work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Establish' reads as proving a fact; here it means to decree or set up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of decreeing: laws and rites are ordained, that is, set up by authority.

entries.clue: Welcome king hosted by uncomplaining prior (10)

indicatorNotes.hosted by: STOICAL plays host, with R inside

blocks.note: a stoic bears hardship without complaint

annotation.surface: A monarch warmly received by a patient monk at his priory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like the monk heading a priory; it is the adjective meaning earlier.
annotation.definitionFit: Historical things belong to an earlier, prior time.

entries.clue: As soon as feasible, empty case (4)

indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: if a plan is on, it is feasible

annotation.surface: An instruction to clear out a suitcase at the earliest opportunity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As soon as feasible' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'As soon as', as in 'once you arrive'.
annotation.definitionFit: Once means as soon as: 'once it stops, we go'.

entries.clue: Inoffensive note received by family (5)

indicatorNotes.received by: something received is taken in, as a guest is received into a house, so CLAN takes E inside

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family

annotation.surface: A harmless letter delivered to a household.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as a message; it is a musical note.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of jokes or language free of obscenity, as in 'keep it clean'.

entries.clue: Jaguar groomed with it’s tongue (8)

indicatorNotes.groomed: groomed fur is rearranged, so the letters are too

blocks.note: used as printed, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A big cat licking its coat clean with its tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe looks like a misprint for 'its'; ''s' is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition. The tongue is a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Gujarati is a language of western India, a tongue.

entries.clue: Men accepting such charity would be new (3)

indicatorNotes.accepting: MEN takes the answer inside it

blocks.note: the container, MEN, that the answer goes into; it gives no letters of the answer
the result, MAIDEN, is defined as new; it gives no letters of the answer
the answer itself: put inside MEN it makes MAIDEN, which means new

annotation.surface: A proud observation that men who took handouts would be born again.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay works backwards: M(AID)EN spells MAIDEN, and a maiden voyage is a new one. 'Such' stands for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: foreign aid and charity both mean help given freely to those in need.

entries.clue: One displaces equestrian in tournament, taking the lead (6)

indicatorNotes.taking the lead: the lead, or first letter, is taken away

blocks.note: a JOUSTER without its first letter

annotation.surface: A knight who unseats a rival in the lists and goes ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking the lead' reads as going in front; it removes the lead letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An ouster is one who ousts, one who displaces.

entries.clue: Dull animal’s home beside meadow (6)

blocks.note: a den is a wild animal's lair

annotation.surface: A boring lair beside a field.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse of the clue's order: the meadow comes first. Lea is a poetic word for a meadow, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: lead is grey and heavy, so leaden skies or leaden prose are dull.

entries.clue: All truly concerning in banks of Europe (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so VERY ON sits inside the two Es
indicatorNotes.banks of: the banks of a river are its edges, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: very = truly, as in 'the very truth'

annotation.surface: A sweeping claim about everything to do with European banks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks financial next to Europe; it means the edges of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when speaking of people: 'all were invited' and 'everyone was invited' say the same.
